title: Not just a pretty keel: interpreting diversity patterns of Calliotropidae (Vetigastropoda: Seguenzioidea) in Australian deep waters through integrative taxonomy
content:
Abstract
The vetigastropod family Calliotropidae is an important and yet poorly understood component of deep-water benthic communities. In this study, the group is investigated through an integrative approach for the first time, with the aim of resolving its systematics in the Australian deep sea. Analyses of concatenated mitochondrial and nuclear DNA sequences revealed the existence in the region of eight clades, treated as primary species hypotheses (PSHs). Following additional evaluation of shell and radular features, as well as examination of geographic and bathymetric ranges, these PSHs were converted to secondary species hypotheses (SSHs). Our data suggested that Calliotropis and Solaricida represent two well-differentiated genera. Solaricida, here removed from the synonymy of Calliotropis, is distinguished by having an epipodial cylinder. Three species are assigned to Solaricida, one of which is new (Solaricida vorago sp. nov.). In addition, five species of Calliotropis are recognized, one being new (Calliotropis montismarini sp. nov.). Bathybembix abyssorum is transferred to Calliotropis based on its close phylogenetic relationships with other species in this genus. Based on the evidence available, the most likely speciation mechanisms involved are evaluated in the attempt to explain the diversity patterns of calliotropids in Australian deep waters.
